cards.explanation: The answer is sorrow. Jesus says, “…your hearts are filled with sorrow because I have told you these things.” (John 16:6) He also says none of them asks Him where He is going (John 16:5).

The answer is that if He goes, He will send the Advocate. Jesus says, “Unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send Him to you.” (John 16:7) That's the benefit He's talking about. It sounds backwards at first, and I'd have squinted at it too, friends.

The answer is that they do not believe in Him. Jesus says the Advocate will convict the world in regard to sin, “…because they do not believe in Me…” (John 16:9) He gives that reason and no other. Short and clear, just how I like my recipe cards.

The answer is True. Jesus says the Advocate will convict the world in regard to judgment, “…because the prince of this world has been condemned.” (John 16:11) That's the reason He gives. Three things on the list, friends, and each one comes with its own because.

The answer is the Spirit of truth. Jesus says, “…when the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all truth.” (John 16:13) The disciples can't bear everything yet, so the Spirit does the guiding. A guide is a good thing to have when you can't carry the whole load at once.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “…He will not speak on His own, but He will speak what He hears, and He will declare to you what is to come.” (John 16:13) So the Spirit speaks what He hears. No making it up as He goes, friends.

The answer is that the Spirit will glorify Him. Jesus says, “He will glorify Me by taking from what is Mine and disclosing it to you.” (John 16:14) The Spirit takes what is Jesus' and shows it to them. All of it points back to Jesus.

The answer is Father. Jesus says, “Everything that belongs to the Father is Mine.” (John 16:15) That's why He says the Spirit will take from what is His and disclose it. Everything the Father has belongs to Jesus.

The answer is that they ask one another what He means. Some of His disciples “…asked one another…” what He meant, and then they kept asking (John 16:17-18). They say, “We do not understand what He is saying.” (John 16:18) It's a group chat with no answers, friends, just everybody typing.

The answer is False. Verse 19 says, “Aware that they wanted to question Him, Jesus said to them…” (John 16:19) He knew what was on their minds, and He brought it up Himself. They didn't even have to ask.
The answer is joy. Jesus says, “You will grieve, but your grief will turn to joy.” (John 16:20) He says it right after telling them they will “…weep and wail…” Joy is the word He gives them.

The answer is forgets. Jesus says, “…when she brings forth her child, she forgets her anguish because of her joy that a child has been born into the world.” (John 16:21) The joy is that big. Jesus uses her as a picture of how their grief will turn.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “So also you have sorrow now, but I will see you again and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy.” (John 16:22) That's a joy nobody can take. I wish my cookie jar came with that promise, friends.
The answer is so their joy may be complete. Jesus says, “Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.” (John 16:24) That's His reason for telling them to ask. Complete joy is the goal.

The answer is that He will tell them plainly about the Father. Jesus says, “An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you this way, but will tell you plainly about the Father.” (John 16:25) The figures of speech give way to plain talk. I think that's good news for anybody who's squinted at a hard saying.

The two answers are loved and believed. Jesus says, “For the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me and have believed that I came from God.” (John 16:27) Loved is the first blank and believed is the second. They sit right next to each other in the same verse, friends.

The answer is True. The disciples say, “See, now You are speaking plainly and without figures of speech.” (John 16:29) I bet they feel like they're finally getting it. I know that feeling, and it's a good one.

The answer is that they will scatter and leave Him all alone, and it's a heavy one. Jesus says, “…you will be scattered, each to his own home, and you will leave Me all alone.” (John 16:32) The same disciples who just said they believe will scatter. Jesus knew it, and He told them anyway.

The answer is that the Father is with Him. Jesus says, “Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.” (John 16:32) The disciples will leave Him all alone, but He names the Father as the reason He isn't alone.

The answer is that He has overcome the world. Jesus says, “In the world you will have tribulation. But take courage; I have overcome the world!” (John 16:33) He doesn't hide the trouble. He gives the reason for courage right after it. That kind of honesty is something I'd happily follow into any kitchen, friends.
